messages:
Alex: Heads up — after enabling INT8 mixed kernels for rllama-13b on Dedicated, we saw ~11-14% p99 token latency regression on short chats (~8 tokens). perf-bot flagged it.
perf-bot: regression detected: model=rllama-13b variant=int8_mixed metric=p99_token_latency delta=+12.3% run=2026-02-23T15:04:12Z
Alex: Uploaded a quick nvprof snippet. The suspicious bits look like memcpy + kernel launch stalls during layer transitions.
Kevin: can you paste the profile snippet inline? are we hitting fallback kernels that do dequant->compute->requant mid-sequence?
Alex: snippet:
```
GPU memcpy HtoD 0.9ms
kernel int8_gemm 1.2ms
kernel fp16_gemm 0.4ms (fallback)
kernel dequantize + quantize 0.8ms
```
Alex: summary: some layers select INT8 kernels, others fallback to FP16. That causes KV cache to be materialized in FP16 for parts of the sequence and converted back, which looks costly.
Simone: yep — conversion overhead + extra memcpy is killer for short-context p99. We saw a similar pattern in perf-run #4821. Also our batching heuristic flips when kernel latency variance > 2x, leading to smaller batches.
Marta: quick question — were embeddings and lm_head quantized in this run? Excluding them usually avoids conversions on prefix writes.
Kevin: they were included. On a local A/B, excluding embeddings+lm_head recovered ~6% p99. But calibration quality mattered too — a bad calibration increases fallback rate.
Simone: calibration note: if activation distributions in live traffic diverge from the calibration corpus, quant ranges clip or saturate -> runtime opts for safer FP16 kernels or triggers per-layer fallbacks. We should try percentile-based calibration and also per-layer live rescaling.
Alex: I opened PR #6032 to add kernel_fallback_count and expose per-layer quant_mode in traces so we can correlate. Running an experiment now.
Marta: another lever — batching heuristic. Today we compute batch windows by predicted latency variance. If a kernel switch is likely mid-batch we should either pin variant for the batch or prefer kernels that keep KV in-place. Maybe add a routing policy "pin_variant_per_batch".
Kevin: +1. Also consider preferring 4-bit kernels for attention that operate in-place (no dequant) even if pure single-kernel latency is slightly higher; end-to-end p99 improves.
Simone: proposed experiment plan:
1) live-sample calibration (10k tokens) instead of static corpora
2) exclude embeddings & lm_head from quantization
3) enable pin_variant_per_batch routing policy
4) record kernel_fallback_count, p50/p95/p99, and memcpy time
I'll run it on a small Dedicated pool today and post numbers.
Alex: if we still see >8% regression after pinning, roll back mixed-int8 default for Dedicated; keep it opt-in until we stabilize. @Marta please draft release note.
Marta: on it. I'll also add a Console hint recommending "live calibration" for Dedicated customers when enabling mixed quant.
Kevin: FYI I pushed a micro-optimization that fuses dequant memcpy into the kernel to avoid an extra device->device copy. PR #6038. Could cut conversion overhead ~35%.
perf-bot: perf test summary: baseline -> int8_mixed_with_pin: p99 -3.5%, fallback_count 4; int8_mixed_no_pin: p99 +9.8%, fallback_count 31
Alex: awesome numbers. If Simone's run matches, let's merge pinning + fused kernel after a quick canary. Thanks team :rocket:
Marta: tagging infra for canary scheduling. I'll also add a short how-to for customers about per-layer excludes and calibration tips.
Simone: will post the detailed traces (kernel_fallback_count per layer) once the run finishes. Expecting results in ~30m.
Kevin: one more thing — add a small metric for "kv_materialize_bytes" so we can track how often we re-materialize KV in a different dtype. That will make root-cause queries easier.
Alex: good call. Added a ticket to product infra.
Marta: thanks, everyone. Keep the thread updated and @channel if rollback needed.
